items.label: system: coding assistant instructions
items.text: You are a coding assistant. Answer in Python 3. Answer with a short explanation first, then code. Never invent library functions that do not exist. If the user asks for something ambiguous, pick the most common interpretation and say what you assumed. Keep answers under 300 words unless the user asks for more detail.

items.label: examples: two few-shot Q&A pairs
items.text: Example 1 — Q: How do I reverse a list in place? A: Use list.reverse(), which mutates the list and returns None. Example 2 — Q: How do I read a JSON file? A: Use json.load(open('data.json')) inside a with block so the file closes. Both answers are short, show real code, and name the exact function used.

items.label: retrieved: pathlib docs chunk
items.text: From the project docs: pathlib.Path.read_text() reads a file as text and returns a string. Path.write_text(data) writes it back. Path.glob('*.py') yields matching paths. Use Path(__file__).parent to locate files relative to the current module instead of relying on the working directory, which changes depending on how the script is launched.

items.label: retrieved: argparse docs chunk
items.text: From the project docs: argparse.ArgumentParser builds a command-line interface. add_argument('--budget', type=int) parses an integer flag. parse_args() reads sys.argv. Use choices=[...] to restrict a flag to known values, and default= to set the value used when the flag is absent. Errors print usage and exit with code 2.

items.label: retrieved: testing notes chunk
items.text: From the team wiki: keep tests in test_*.py next to the module. Use unittest, no extra framework, so tests run with python3 -m unittest. Each test should assert one behaviour and name it in the test method. Tests must pass without network access, without a GPU, and without paid APIs, so CI can run them on a free runner.

items.label: history: 6 earlier turns
items.text:
User: I want a tool that packs LLM context into a token budget.
Assistant: Sure — I will build a packer with must-include items, priority ordering, and three overflow policies.
User: Make it stdlib only, no API keys and no downloads.
Assistant: Done — token counts are a chars/4 estimate, clearly labelled, and everything runs offline.
User: Add a history compaction step that keeps the latest turn intact.
Assistant: Added — compaction keeps the first sentence of each older turn plus the full latest turn.
User: Now run it on the example and show me what was dropped and why.
Assistant: Running it now with an 800-token budget and the compact policy.
